% Generate a Python module that turns a stated health goal and a short profile
% into a structured, safety-bounded plan.
%
% Canonical source for the `fitness_app` module. A stale copy once lived at
% fitness/fitness_app_python.prompt with weaker R4/R5/R6 wording; it was deleted
% (recoverable at git 1d7a1f2 in that directory) so this file is the only source
% of truth. Generate with:
%   pdd generate prompts/fitness_app_python.prompt
% Tests live at tests/test_fitness_app.py and name the rule each one enforces.

<include>context/project_preamble.prompt</include>

<responsibility>
Asks the user which goal they are pursuing — Weight Loss or Prevent Diabetes —
collects a short profile, and computes a structured plan tailored to that goal.
Planning is a pure function of the profile; the intake layer is a thin shell
over an injected prompt callable.
</responsibility>

<non_responsibilities>
- Does not diagnose, screen for, or rule out any medical condition.
- Does not persist, transmit, or log the profile. Health data leaves no trace.
- Does not read the system clock. Age is supplied, never derived from a
  birthdate and "today".
- Does not track progress over time, store history, or compare against a
  previous run. Each call is a single stateless evaluation.
- Does not prescribe specific foods, supplements, drugs, or macronutrient
  splits beyond the protein target R7 defines.
</non_responsibilities>

<vocabulary>
- BMR: resting energy expenditure in kcal/day, by Mifflin-St Jeor.
- TDEE: BMR scaled by an activity multiplier — total daily burn in kcal/day.
- Deficit: TDEE minus the recommended intake. Always non-negative; a plan never
  recommends eating above maintenance.
- Calorie floor: the lowest daily intake this module will ever recommend —
  1500 kcal for male profiles, 1200 for female. Below this, a self-directed
  diet stops being safe without supervision, so the floor is a hard clamp and
  not a default.
- Floored profile: one whose TDEE is below its own calorie floor — a small,
  older, or sedentary body that burns less in a day than the floor allows it
  to eat. No safe self-directed deficit exists; such a plan carries a zero
  deficit and refers the user onward rather than inventing a smaller cut. At
  TDEE exactly equal to the floor the ordinary arithmetic already lands on the
  floor with a zero deficit, so no special case is needed there.
- Healthy-weight ceiling: the body mass at BMI 24.9 for the profile's height.
  24.9 rather than 25.0 so the target stays inside the healthy band under the
  rounding R3 mandates.
- Risk score: an additive tally of diabetes risk factors, loosely modeled on
  the ADA risk test. It is a triage prompt to seek testing, never a result.
- Unsupervised claim: any statement that a user does or does not have a
  condition, or that a plan will prevent one. Forbidden by R9.
</vocabulary>

<contract_rules>
R1 (MUST): Accept exactly two goals. `parse_goal` recognizes "1"/"2", and the
full goal names case-insensitively and surrounding-whitespace-insensitively.
Anything else — a third number, an empty string, a prefix like "weight" — is
unrecognized and returns `None`.

R2 (MUST NOT): Never default, guess, or coerce an unrecognized goal into a
valid one. `run_intake` re-asks until a recognized answer arrives. Rationale: a
plan silently built for the goal the user did not choose is worse than no plan.

R3 (MUST): Compute BMI rounded to one decimal, and categorize *that rounded
value*, so the number shown and the band named can never disagree. Bands are
lower-inclusive: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to under 25 healthy, 25 to under
30 overweight, 30 and above obese.

R4 (MUST NOT): Never recommend a daily intake below the profile's calorie
floor, on any input, for any goal. The clamp is unconditional — no combination
of age, size, sex, or activity may produce a target under the floor. This
binds even when TDEE itself falls below the floor: the plan reports the floor,
not the smaller burn, because the floor is the lowest intake this module is
willing to name.

R5 (MUST): For an unfloored profile, recommend `min(tdee, max(tdee - 500,
floor))` kcal/day and derive the reported deficit as `tdee - target` from that
clamped figure. The nominal 500 is an aspiration, not a reported fact: when
the floor binds, the plan reports the smaller deficit it actually achieves,
never the 500 it wanted. For a floored profile the formula would return a
sub-floor target and so does not apply: recommend the floor itself and report
a deficit of zero rather than the negative figure `tdee - floor` would give.
A floored plan says plainly that no safe self-directed deficit exists at this
profile's daily burn and that a clinician or dietitian should set the target,
and it carries that referral among its actions. Under no branch may the
reported deficit be negative.

R6 (MUST): Project weekly loss as `deficit * 7 / 7700` kg, and weeks-to-target
as the kilograms above the healthy-weight ceiling divided by that rate. Each
of the three figures is omitted (`None`) exactly when it would otherwise be
degenerate, and not otherwise: the rate when the deficit is zero, since a zero
rate is not a projection; the kilogram gap when the profile is already at or
under the ceiling, since a non-positive gap is not a distance to travel; the
timeline when either of those holds, since it would divide by zero or count
down a gap that does not exist. A profile under the ceiling with a real
deficit still reports its weekly rate — it is losing at a knowable pace, it
simply has no ceiling left to reach. No figure is ever reported as zero,
negative, or infinite in place of being omitted. The three conditions are
independent and must not be collapsed into one branch: a single test covering
both the zero-deficit and the at-ceiling case will pass against an
implementation that omits the rate whenever either holds, which R6 forbids.

R7 (MUST): Set the protein target at 1.6 g per kg of current body mass,
rounded to the nearest gram.

R8 (MUST): Score diabetes risk additively: age 60+ scores 3 and age 45-59
scores 2 — never both; BMI 30+ scores 3 and BMI 25 to under 30 scores 2 —
never both; family history 2; high blood pressure 2; a sedentary activity
level 2. Band the total: 6 and above high, 3 to 5 moderate, under 3 low. Every
factor that scored is named in the result. The 7%-of-body-mass loss target
appears when, and only when, BMI is 25 or above.

R9 (MUST NOT): Never state or imply a diagnosis, a screening result, or a
guarantee of prevention, and never omit the disclaimer. Every rendered plan
carries it. This holds for the high-risk branch too: that branch may recommend
asking a clinician for an A1C test, and may not suggest what such a test would
show.

R10 (MUST): Raise `ValueError` for a profile outside plausible human bounds —
age 13-100, weight 25-400 kg, height 100-250 cm — and for any non-finite
measurement. NaN compares false against every bound, so a range check alone
admits it silently; test for finiteness explicitly. This is the one input error
that raises rather than returning a plan.

R11 (MUST NOT): Keep `plan_for` and everything beneath it pure — no I/O, no
clock read, no argument mutation, no logging. Only `run_intake` and `main`
touch the outside world, and only through their injected callables. Rationale:
the arithmetic above is safety-bearing and must be reproducible under test
without a terminal.

R12 (MUST): Expose the floored-profile referral R5 requires as structured
data, not as prose only — a `WeightLossDetail.is_floored: bool` that is true
exactly when the profile is floored. A referral discoverable only by matching
substrings in rendered text cannot be asserted on without coupling the test to
wording, so the flag is the contract and the sentence is its presentation.
Every floored plan carries both.

R13 (MUST): Render every plan to non-empty text on every reachable branch,
including a floored plan whose three projections are all `None`. Omitted
figures are omitted from the prose, never rendered as "None", "0", "nan", or an
empty field. Rationale: R6 makes absence routine, so absence must have a
presentation.
</contract_rules>

<interface_notes>
- `plan_for(profile) -> Plan` is the documented entry point for computation.
  `run_intake(ask, *, show=None) -> Profile` is the entry point for collection;
  `ask` is a `Callable[[str], str]` and `show` a `Callable[[str], None]`,
  defaulting to `input` and `print`. Tests inject fakes and never touch a
  terminal.
- `main(ask=input, show=print) -> int` wires intake to planning to rendering
  and returns a process exit code. It is the only symbol that may catch
  `KeyboardInterrupt`/`EOFError`.
- `render(plan) -> str` returns the full user-facing text and performs no
  output itself, so tests can assert on it directly.
- `Profile` is a frozen dataclass validated in `__post_init__`, so an invalid
  profile cannot exist. `Plan`, `Metrics`, `WeightLossDetail`, and
  `DiabetesRisk` are frozen too.
- `Plan` carries `goal`, `metrics`, `headline`, `actions: tuple[str, ...]`, and
  exactly one of `weight_loss` / `risk` — the detail for the other goal is
  `None`, so a plan cannot carry the wrong goal's numbers.
- `WeightLossDetail`: `target_kcal`, `deficit_kcal`, `weekly_loss_kg`,
  `kg_above_ceiling`, `weeks_to_ceiling`, `protein_g`, `is_floored`. The three
  projections are optional per R6; `is_floored` is the R12 flag.
- `DiabetesRisk`: `score`, `band`, `factors: tuple[str, ...]`,
  `seven_percent_kg` (optional per R8).
- Enums for every closed set: `Goal`, `Sex`, `Activity` (carrying its
  multiplier), `BmiCategory`, `RiskBand`.
- `DISCLAIMER` is a module-level constant so tests assert against one string.
- Parsers `parse_goal`, `parse_sex`, `parse_activity`, `parse_yes_no` each
  return `None` on unrecognized input rather than raising or guessing; the
  re-ask loop in `run_intake` is the sole place that decides what to do about
  it.
</interface_notes>

<pdd-interface>
{"type":"module","module":{"functions":[
  {"name":"plan_for","signature":"(profile: Profile) -> Plan","returns":"Plan"},
  {"name":"compute_metrics","signature":"(profile: Profile) -> Metrics","returns":"Metrics"},
  {"name":"run_intake","signature":"(ask, *, show=None) -> Profile","returns":"Profile"},
  {"name":"render","signature":"(plan: Plan) -> str","returns":"str"},
  {"name":"parse_goal","signature":"(raw: str) -> Goal | None","returns":"Goal | None"},
  {"name":"main","signature":"(ask=input, show=print) -> int","returns":"int"}]}}
</pdd-interface>
